fillers: Myeongdong means 'bright town' — and by night it truly lives up to the name, a canyon of glowing signs and endless energy.
Everything around you is packed into just a few blocks. Myeongdong is one of the most visited neighbourhoods in all of Seoul.
As you walk, notice the cosmetics shops on every corner. This is the birthplace of the K-beauty boom — free samples are practically a sport here.
By evening these lanes fill with street-food carts: tornado potatoes, grilled lobster, egg bread, and hotteok sizzling in the cold air.
Listen for the shop staff calling out in Korean, Chinese, and Japanese. Myeongdong has welcomed travellers from all over Asia for decades.
The name of the game here is layers of retail — flagship stores at street level, hidden cafes upstairs, and bargain basements below.
Many of these streets are pedestrian-only, so take your time. In Myeongdong, wandering without a plan is half the fun.
Look up now and then. Above the neon, you'll spot older brick buildings that survived from Seoul's early modern era.
If your feet get tired, duck into any building — most have a cafe with a view over the crowds below.
Myeongdong sits right between Namsan Mountain and the old city centre, so grand landmarks are only a short walk in any direction.
Weekends here get shoulder-to-shoulder busy. Locals say if you can shop in Myeongdong on a Saturday, you can shop anywhere.
Hungry? Go ahead — nearly every street-food stall here takes cards and mobile pay these days, so nothing stands between you and that tteokbokki.
You're walking one of Korea's most famous shopping streets, roughly a kilometre of pure retail from the station to Euljiro.
Take a mental snapshot. This blend of neon, food smells, and constant motion is the Myeongdong every traveller remembers.
